statement: The census read all 29 files of organism/gen-0 (485992 lines) as text and ran it in 3 shards of 1 cells files, one at a time, each shard loading only its own cells (mode cut: an owned cell misses the mail of every cell outside its shard, so this is an approximation and never the bar), under a cap of 8000 MB resident per shard; peak rss per shard 1042.8 MB, 1093.9 MB, 1056.4 MB, wall 8.7 s. It drove the organism 20 ticks with nothing injected, then ran the hosted algebra and sequence problems (68 more ticks; algebra 34 of 36, sequence 0 of 22). Of 40000 declared cells 31403 ran (78.51 percent) and 13680 emitted; of 440578 declared edges 132406 delivered (30.05 percent). Of 485585 declaration lines 168816 declared something that ran or delivered and 316769 are dead; 169223 of 485992 lines are load bearing (34.82 percent). Not exact: cut shards.
drive: one brain.tick(1) per event loop turn per shard, nothing injected, runtime/kernels.mjs installed; then the hosted algebra and sequence problems into the cells the whole organism picks (tasks/host.mjs nameCells), on every shard, with the whole schedule

ratio.how: peak rss of 76 progress samples up to tick 86

live.phases: the drive ticks plus the hosted algebra and sequence problems, sharded cut
